title: Single case-control design for the study of the neuropsychological deficits and dissociations in Huntington’s disease-like 2
author: Ferreira-Correia, Anderson, et al.
materials: RAVLT Delayed trial and Recognition Trial,
SWCIT, 15), Visual Reproduction II Sub-Test, and

steps.title: Obtain consent and genetic counseling
steps.instruction: Meet each participant with an independent genetic counsellor who explains the study and obtains formal written consent (for patients) or direct consent (for healthy controls). Record any refusals or inability to participate in specific components (e.g., MRI or neuropsychological testing).

steps.title: Neurological exam and blood draw
steps.instruction: Perform the neurological assessment required by the study, then collect a blood sample from the participant before proceeding to further testing.

steps.title: Neuropsychological assessment (2‑hour limit)
steps.instruction: Administer the full battery of cognitive tests within a maximum of two hours, offering a break after the RAVLT recognition trial. Conduct all testing in a well‑lit, ventilated, quiet room on a flat surface (table or desk).

substeps.instruction: 1. Demographic questionnaire (age, education, occupation, language experience, gender, ancestry, HDL2 history, medical history, medication).
2. Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) – English 7.1 version (Lion, Rhinoceros, Camel, Version); approx. 10 min; add one point for participants with <12 years of education.
3. Rey Auditory Verbal Learning Test (RAVLT) – lists A–B; approx. 20 min; administer trials I–V, trial B, trial VI, then delayed trial and recognition trial later in the sequence.
4. Design Fluency Test (D‑KEFS) – three unstructured design trials, 60 s each; assess non‑verbal fluency, flexibility, inhibition.
5. Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT) – substitution task for 90 s; first form written, second form oral; assesses divided attention, visual scanning, motor speed.
6. Hooper Visual Organization Test (HVOT) – 30 cut‑up object pictures to be recognised and named.
7. Spatial Addition Sub‑test (WMS‑IV) – visual working memory task using sequential grids (no fixed time limit reported).
8. RAVLT delayed recall trial followed immediately by the recognition trial (break offered after recognition).
9. Visual Reproduction I (WMS‑IV) – view design for 10 s then draw from memory (immediate non‑verbal memory).
10. Letter‑Number Sequencing (WAIS‑IV) – 7 items, each with 3 oral trials; approx. 10 min; assesses verbal working memory.
11. Symbol Search (WAIS‑IV) – mark ‘yes’ or ‘no’ for target symbols within groups; complete as many items as possible in 120 s; assesses visual attention and processing speed.
12. Controlled Oral‑Word Association Test (COWAT) – three letter‑fluency trials (F, A, S); 1 min per trial; assess verbal fluency.
13. Tower Test (D‑KEFS) – build target tower using discs of varying size; move one disc at a time, never place larger disc on smaller; no time limit specified.

14. Stroop Word‑Colour Interference Test (SWCIT) – three pages (Word Reading, Colour Naming, Colour‑Word Reading) each with 100 items (5 columns × 20 items); 45 s per page; approx. 5 min total; measures selective attention, cognitive flexibility, inhibition.
15. Visual Reproduction II (WMS‑IV) – after an interference interval, draw the same designs again and select the matching one from six alternatives (delayed non‑verbal memory).
16. Purdue Grooved Pegboard Test (PGPT) – place pegs as quickly as possible in a row of holes; first trial with dominant hand, second trial with non‑dominant hand.

steps.title: MRI scanning
steps.instruction: Transport the participant to the MRI facility (University of the Witwatersrand Donald Gordon Medical Centre). Provide lunch upon arrival. Acquire structural MRI on a 1.5 T Philips Intera MR scanner (Philips Medical Systems, Eindhoven).

steps.title: Record observations
steps.instruction: Keep behavioral and clinical notes throughout the entire assessment (including any interruptions, breaks, or deviations from the planned order).

steps.title: Deficit statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Compare each participant’s raw test scores to the matched control group using the Crawford‑Howell modified t‑test (one‑tailed, p < 0.05). Use the program Singlims_ES.exe to obtain point estimates, effect sizes (Zcc), and the percentage of controls scoring lower than the case. If covariates are to be considered, repeat the analysis with BTD_Cov.exe.

steps.title: Dissociation statistical analysis
steps.instruction: Assess intra‑case variability with the Revised Standardized Difference Test (RSDT) using Dissoc_ES.exe (two‑tailed, p < 0.05). Identify classical dissociations (one test within normal limits, another with a deficit) and strong dissociations (both tests with deficits, one significantly lower than the other). Record effect sizes and percentages as per Crawford et al. guidelines.
